## Conclusions
- **Most of the gain is not RefCOCOg-specific.** Training only on RefCOCO + RefCOCO+ captions (8,754 images,
  37.5k captions; collected with the interactive ReferIt game, shorter and terser than RefCOCOg) and testing on the
  RefCOCOg-derived folds still gives **84.36 (+12.98)**, vs. 87.34 (+15.96) with all three sources (010).
  So about 13 of the 16 points carry across annotation sources and caption styles. About 3 points come from
  RefCOCOg-style captions, which partly reflects the shared style with our validation folds and partly that
  010 had 1.8× more images.
- **LPCVC sample:** 92.01 (vs 91.37 for 010 and 88.91 pretrained). All differences are within noise on 56 images.
- **Takeaway for the report:** the domain adaptation effect (object-level, attribute-style referring
  captions) is real and transfers across datasets. The headline +16 on our validation set should be quoted
  together with this +13 cross-source number as a more conservative estimate.
- **Decision:** keep training on all three sources for the submission (more data, same domain). Use this
  number as the conservative estimate in the report.
